name: POST /api/leadflow/segments/:id/compute - the audit snapshot
description:
Computes the audience and CAPTURES IT AT RUN START (73357dd8-628f-47fa-9e41-1b42cf1f23fc#AC3). Derived later it would be a different set - people convert, consent lapses, records are suppressed - so "who was in this audience" is only answerable if it was written down at the moment it mattered.

THE REFUSALS ARE STORED ALONGSIDE THE MEMBERS. "Who did we message" is answerable from the members alone; "why was this person not messaged" is what a consent complaint or a rights audit actually asks, and that answer exists only if the exclusions were kept.

THE SNAPSHOT NAMES THE VERSION THAT PRODUCED IT, denormalised rather than joined (73357dd8-628f-47fa-9e41-1b42cf1f23fc#AC4). The join gives the same answer today and a DIFFERENT one after the definition is superseded, and "who was in this audience and under what rule" must not change retroactively.

QA: measured live against the definition created earlier in the chain.

testCases.name: The audience is snapshotted with its members, refusals and the version used
NEGATIVE: no segment with that id
NEGATIVE: no Authorization header at all
NEGATIVE: a bearer token that does not verify

errorCases.message: candidates must be a non-empty array of { subject_ref }
errorCases.when: the candidate list is absent or empty.

errorCases.message: No segment definition with that id
errorCases.when: the segment id does not exist.

errorCases.message: Authorization header with a bearer token is required
errorCases.when: the Authorization header is absent, empty, or uses a scheme other than Bearer.

errorCases.message: Session token is invalid or expired
errorCases.when: a Bearer token was presented but does not verify.
